correctness.rationale: For n=3p, the explicit CRT vertices A_t=(1,g^t), B_t=(2,c g^t) partition U(3p), and their two cyclic difference classes are (2,(1-c)g^t) and (1,(c-g)g^t), each a complete unit fiber since c differs from 1 and g. For m odd and q|m odd prime, the even-length existing cycle lifts by y_{rL+i}=x_i+m alpha_i r with alternating alpha_i in {1,2}. Every vertex fiber and every oriented difference fiber has nonzero slope modulo q, including the closing edge. Induction in q=3 and q=p gives all a,b>=1. The replay checks 137 finite moduli but is not relied on for universal quantification.

originality.rationale: The 2013-origin Sun paper, Theorem 1.4 and Remark 1.4 (read in full around the relevant proof), establishes only prime-power moduli and states the general odd-modulus case as conjectural. The composite family 3^a p^b has two distinct prime divisors; the CRT alternation and odd-prime lift are not consequences of the given primitive-root cycle. The 1975 Hugo S. Sun paper was inspected and treats multiplicative group decomposition, not the required directed Hamiltonian difference labelling. Targeted mathematical literature, semantic-record, and OEIS queries did not yield a covering theorem; this is best-knowledge originality, not a claim of exhaustive bibliographic priority.

value.rationale: The result supplies an infinite two-prime-support family of previously conjectured reduced-residue cyclic difference permutations, with a uniform constructive lift across all exponents. Noncyclicity of U(3p) prevents the existing primitive-root prime-power cycle from directly covering this base family; the alternating CRT method is structurally motivated. This gives a substantive partial case of the odd-modulus conjecture and a reusable lifting theorem rather than a finite example extension.
